name: acme-default-plan
source: The four ACME templates, docs/reference/examples/acme/templates/, as the section loader contract's fixtures hold them (contracts/section/loader/testdata/acme-*.section.json), given out of order. The five plan variables are the plan variables of docs/reference/examples/acme/acme.obk.yaml, one with a default and one with options. 0030, The default plan: the axis variables and every template as a section, with no answers. Hashes: shasum -a 256 over a canonical text written by hand from the section hasher contract (Canonical form, Fields, Defaults, Prose, Strings), the four acme-*.canonical.json files. The ACME plan file records no real hash for them.

name: hasher-goldens
source: Five sections and their hashes from the golden cases of contracts/section/hasher/testdata/cases.json (full, basic, prose, sets, unknown-fields), copied with their canonical texts and given out of order. The full section has a source that must be replaced by the new one. The basic section has no timing and no variable type, and its plan section keeps them absent while its hash is of the defaults. The unknown-fields section keeps its unknown fields. 0030, Identifiers: the source hash is computed by the tool when it copies a template into a plan. The axis variables are those of the 0030 sketch.

name: byte-order
source: Contract rule: Order. Six sections, given out of order. Id order differs from title order, from timing order (b is before-day-one, a-b is week-one), from the order after gives (a comes after b), from length, and from number order (10-x before 9-x). Hashes: shasum -a 256 over a canonical text written by hand from the section hasher contract, the byte-order-*.canonical.json files.

name: values-as-given
source: Domain model, Provenance: templateSet is the build's sha or tag and generatedOn is a date a driver passes in, because the core never reads a clock. Values that differ from the other cases show that the plan holds what it was given. Hash from the hasher golden case basic.

name: section-clauses
source: 0050, A condition can test whether a section is on: the instantiator copies a section clause as loaded, in includeIf and in a variable's askIf, with both enabled true and enabled false. The canonical text is written by hand from the hasher rules and 0050, which hashes the clause as {"section":"id","enabled":true}, and its hash is shasum -a 256 over that text. A section clause that is dropped or changed in the copy, or an enabled false that is lost, changes the plan.

name: no-templates
source: Contract rule: Empty inputs. 0030, The default plan: the axis variables plus every template as a section. With no template there is no section, and the axis variables are still there.

name: no-axis-variables
source: Contract rule: Empty inputs. The variables a plan holds are the ones given, and none given means none. Hash from the hasher golden case basic.

name: nothing-given
source: Contract rule: Empty inputs. The plan still has its version and its provenance.

name: duplicate-ids
source: 0030, Identifiers: a template id is stable and answers are kept by section id, so two sections with one id cannot both be in a plan. Contract rule: Problems. Three sections share a, two share b, with a pair identical and a third different, and c is alone. The problems come in id order, one for each id.

name: nameless-axis-variables
source: Domain model, Variable: a name is what an answer is kept under. Contract rule: Problems. Two of the four variables have no name, one with a description and one with nothing. The index counts from zero in the list given.

name: both-problems
source: Contract rule: Problems. Every problem is reported, the template problems first, and no plan is returned.

name: single-duplicate-id
source: Contract rule: Problems. One id repeats, so exactly one problem, with a count of 2, and no plan. Kills an implementation that returns the plan when it finds a single problem, such as a test of len(problems) > 1.

name: single-nameless-axis-variable
source: Contract rule: Problems. One variable has no name, so exactly one problem, at index 0, counted from zero, and no plan. Kills an implementation that returns the plan when it finds a single problem, and an index counted from one.

name: single-duplicate-and-single-nameless
source: Contract rule: Problems. One problem of each kind, template problem first. Kills an implementation that reports only one kind, and one that puts the variable problem first.

name: variable-example
source: A variable's optional example, an illustration of a good answer, is part of what a template says, so the section is its template copied with the example and the hash covers it. The canonical text is written by hand from the hasher rules, with example right after description and omitted when empty, and its hash is shasum -a 256 over that text. The role example is Engineering manager, from the change brief. A section that loses the example in the copy changes the plan, and a hash that ignores it differs from this one.

name: sub-sections
source: 0070: a template may name a parent, the section is its template copied with the parent as held, and the hash covers the parent, written like any text identifier, omitted when empty, right after includeIf. Three templates given out of order: a root, a sub-section of it with an includeIf on the root's question and a timing, and a sub-section of that one. The canonical texts are written by hand from the hasher rules with parent after includeIf, and each hash is shasum -a 256 over its file. A section that loses the parent in the copy, or a hash that leaves it out or writes it in another place, differs from this one.

name: answer-test-lists
source: Contract rule: Nothing shared. A condition's answer tests are copied at every depth, so an `is` and an `isNot` that hold lists, in includeIf and in a variable's askIf, share nothing with the template. The canonical text is written by hand from the hasher rules (Values: a list is written in the order held, `is` and `isNot` are not sets), and its hash is shasum -a 256 over that file. A copy that leaves the `is` or `isNot` list shared with the argument fails the nothing-shared test on this case.
